annotation.method: Codex freshly reread the complete 47-page local paper for the missing-tier audit, rechecked Algorithms 1-2, equations (3.2)-(3.20), Theorems 3.1-3.4, and Appendices A, C, and D, and compared every T1/T2 candidate with the full frozen Mathlib and NumStability baselines; the existing T3 was retained.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P19 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

corpus_membership: This paper is part of the current corpus listed in metadata/manifest.json.
paper_version: HAL preprint hal-05071696v2, submitted 2026-05-19; IMA Journal of Numerical Analysis, in press, article pages 1-46

rejected_candidates.reason: These establish the computational model and hypotheses rather than a concise selected conclusion. Their error sources are retained only as hypotheses of the selected T3 result.

rejected_candidates.candidate: the complete specialized statement of Theorem 3.2
rejected_candidates.reason: The general modular theorem uses only standard norm facts from the mounted library and therefore does not meet T2. P19-T3 selects the specialized right and flexible results in Theorems 3.3-3.4.
The rho_M and rho_b quantities make a compact exact comparison less clean. The right/flexible pair shares common terms and exposes the paper's critical implementation distinction directly.
This is a property of the synthetic matrix generator used to structure experiments, not the paper's main rounding-error contribution.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Tables 2-3 and the six strategy recommendations in Sections 4.2-4.3
rejected_candidates.reason: Several recommendations combine simplified asymptotic bounds with problem-dependent or explicitly qualified empirical behavior. T3 captures the exact theoretical right/flexible comparison that drives one of the strongest recommendations.
These report finite experiments and iteration counts rather than universally quantified mathematical results.
These are practical experiments whose outliers are explicitly noted as not always explained by the simplified theory.

rejected_candidates.candidate: backward-error, implementation-performance, and industrial-software directions in Section 6
rejected_candidates.reason: The paper identifies these as open issues or future work, not completed results.

T1.decision: Skipped after a fresh full-paper audit. The only isolated reusable perturbation-norm step is an elementary triangle inequality. The operational matrix-vector bounds are quoted from earlier work, and bridging the paper's full MGS/GMRES execution to a NumStability kernel would require a new paper-specific theorem rather than one substantial existing match.

T2.decision: Skipped after a fresh full-paper audit. No theorem aligns with two substantial frozen results: its matrix-vector error equations are externally cited contracts, while the MGS, Arnoldi, preconditioning, and attainable-error assembly has no NumStability counterpart. The remaining reusable norm facts are elementary.

T3.decision: Use Theorems 3.3-3.4 and Remark 4 for right and flexible preconditioned GMRES; NumStability has no corresponding GMRES execution or attainable-error theorem.

selection_policy: Represent the source's unspecified low-degree c(n,k) by its value at the selected dimensions, and parameterize the qualitative second-order semantics instead of inventing polynomial coefficients or an asymptotic variable.
When Section 2 writes an unqualified square condition number, expose the source-authorized Frobenius or induced-2 choice explicitly and apply it consistently to the matrix and its certified inverse.
Represent the paper's four modular error sources and right/flexible precision distinction explicitly.
Do not promote empirical heatmaps, iteration counts, qualified recommendations, or future-work claims to theorem targets.
Keep every public definition free of NumStability imports.
Assign tiers only after comparison with the complete frozen NumStability source and the compiled condition-L bundle recorded in metadata/library_olean.json.
